Name: Ephrem the Syrian
Summary: A fourth-century Syriac-speaking deacon, poet, and teacher from Nisibis and later Edessa, one of the great hymn-writers of the early church.
Contribution: His hymns and poems taught the faith in memorable verse, defended orthodox belief against heresy, and meditated on creation, the incarnation, and paradise, making him a central voice of Syriac Christianity.
KeyWorks: Hymns on the Nativity; Hymns on Paradise
Testimony: Spent his life in teaching, hymn-writing, and service to the poor, including caring for plague victims in Edessa.
